title: Knowing Less After a Diagnostic Test: Dilation in Clinical Decision-Making
abstract: arXiv:2611.20209v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Dilation (Seidenfeld and Wasserman 1993) occurs when conditioning on new information \textit{only} increases uncertainty regardless of what the information reveals. Often viewed as an undesirable feature of models of ambiguity, dilation has sparked sustained debate about belief updating. This paper shows that following established clinical guidance can induce dilation, even for diagnostic tests that meet conventional performance benchmarks. We characterize when a test is dilation-inducing and show that a ubiquitous feature of performance studies -- evaluating tests against an imperfect reference -- creates scope for dilation. To facilitate detection before clinical use and inform regulatory standards, we develop a finite-sample valid hypothesis test of the null that a diagnostic test is dilation-inducing in this context. translated_title: 诊断测试后反而知道得更少：临床决策中的膨胀现象
translated_abstract: 膨胀（Seidenfeld和Wasserman，1993）指的是一种现象：无论新信息揭示了什么内容，以该新信息为条件都只会增加不确定性。膨胀通常被视为模糊性模型的一个不良特性，并引发了关于信念更新的持续辩论。本文表明，遵循既定的临床指导可能诱发膨胀，即使诊断测试满足了常规的性能基准也是如此。我们刻画了测试何时会诱发膨胀，并指出性能研究中一个普遍存在的特征——以不完善的参照标准来评估测试——为膨胀的发生创造了空间。为了便于在临床应用之前进行检测并为监管标准提供参考，我们开发了一个有限样本有效的假设检验，其原假设为诊断测试在此情境下会诱发膨胀。我们将该方法应用于一项有影响力的研究，该研究先于并促进了胸部CT筛查的临床应用……
tldr: 本文证明遵循临床指南进行诊断测试可能诱发“膨胀”现象（即无论测试结果如何都会增加诊断不确定性），刻画了诱发膨胀的条件，指出以不完善参照标准评估测试性能的普遍做法会扩大膨胀风险，并开发了有限样本假设检验方法以便在临床应用前检测这一问题。
en_tdlr: This paper shows that following established clinical guidance can induce dilation—increased uncertainty regardless of test results—even for diagnostic tests meeting conventional benchmarks, characterizes when tests are dilation-inducing, demonstrates that imperfect-reference evaluation creates scope for dilation, and develops a finite-sample hypothesis test to detect this before clinical use.
